label: Figure 25.3: Trade creation (worked example: ceramic tiles, Poland and Spain)
alt: Supply and demand for ceramic tiles in an importing country with two horizontal partner supply lines, with and without a tariff; two shaded triangles show regained world efficiency and regained consumer surplus.
caption: Hypothetical example: Poland imports ceramic tiles from lower-cost Spain. With a tariff the price is P<sub>w+t</sub> = €20: home firms make Q<sub>2</sub> = 80 million m², buyers take Q<sub>3</sub> = 100 million and 20 million are imported. Inside a customs union the tariff goes and the price falls to P<sub>w</sub> = €12: home output falls to Q<sub>1</sub> = 40 million, purchases rise to Q<sub>4</sub> = 140 million and imports rise to 100 million. The shaded triangles are the regained world efficiency and consumer surplus.
